conviction_note: Q3's drivers were published in the July, August and September monthly metrics, and the sell-side models them line by line (Zacks: DARTs 4.27M, NII $1.12B, commissions $588.9M). My own rebuild of the quarter lands within about 1-3% of the $0.66-0.68 EPS bar. What is left to move the stock is commentary: rates (the Fed hiked on Sept 16, adding about $81M a year of NII per 25bp, but the market's odds of an October hike fell from 66% to 16%), October trading activity in a low-VIX market, and margin balances that ended Q3 below their Q2 close. Those roughly offset. The name has sold its last two EPS beats (-0.97% and -3.34%). So p_up is 51, close to a non-result, while abs_move_pct stays near the history's 6.0% median and the 4.45% straddle. impact_sum (+0.15) and impact_scaled (+0.1) agree.
bar: Adjusted EPS $0.66-0.68 on revenue of $1.83-1.87B. Zacks: $0.66 / $1.83B as of 2026-10-12 (https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/gear-interactive-brokers-ibkr-q3-121504839.html). Motley Fool: $0.67 / $1.86B on 2026-10-14 (https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/10/14/interactive-brokers-group-s-next-earnings-report-tomorrow-could-send-the-stock-soaring-here-s-why/). AlphaStreet: $0.67 per its headline (https://news.alphastreet.com/interactive-brokers-group-ibkr-q3-2026-preview-eps-est-0-67-reports-october-15/). Benzinga is said to carry $0.68 / $1.87B. Three sources agree within a cent, so the bar is treated as sourced. The company issues no formal guidance.
positioning_check: Short interest is about 10.3M shares, 2.27% of shares outstanding, about 2.7 days to cover (FINRA settlement 2026-08-31, via https://altindex.com/ticker/ibkr/short-interest, per the sweep row); Equibles shows about 2.0% of float around 2026-08-19. That is not a crowded short. Baseline: 25-delta skew +1.61 vol points (mild put bid), put/call open interest 1.69, straddle 4.45%, priced lean 'balanced'. The stock is -4.69% over 20 days, -2.58% over 5 days and -14.2% from its 52-week high ($98.75). It fell 5.9% on 2026-09-01 on August DARTs and a 4.8% 10-year yield, and 4.78% on 2026-10-07 on September DARTs and a BMO target trim. Sentiment going in is washed-out rather than euphoric, which is unlike the last two beats that were sold.

findings.finding: Q3 commissions rebuilt from company-published DARTs look slightly above consensus. Q3 average DARTs were about 4.27M (July 4.426M, August 4.276M, September 4.111M), against Q2's 4.82M, which produced $673M of commissions ($139.6M per million DARTs; the same ratio was about $148M in Q3 2025). That implies $596-632M against the Zacks consensus of $588.9M, so about $10-40M of revenue upside, roughly +$0.005-0.02 of EPS on a $0.66-0.68 bar. Q2's low 14.7% effective tax rate, if it normalizes, could absorb part of that.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 beat EPS by about 7.8% ($0.69 vs $0.64) on record commissions and the stock moved -0.97% (baseline 2026-07-21). Q3 2025 beat and moved -3.34% (2025-10-16). Q1 2026 was in line at $0.60 and moved -1.9%. This name has not paid for small beats on pre-released lines.
findings.why_not_priced: The DARTs are public, but the consensus commission line ($588.9M) applies a lower revenue per DART than Q2's or Q3 2025's actuals. If the market had priced the higher per-DART figure, the published consensus would sit near $600M+ and EPS estimates would not have drifted down 2.9% over 30 days (AlphaStreet). The gap is small and could be mix (the September commission per cleared order was $2.57).

findings.finding: Consensus other income ($30M, Zacks) looks low against the run-rate. Q2 2026 other income was $79M, or $66M excluding gains, losses and the currency strategy (Q2 call), and Q3 2025 was $85M. The currency basket (GLOBAL) fell only 0.08% in Q3 per the September metrics release, so the currency drag on comprehensive earnings is small. In Q2, a 0.21% decline still produced a $21M gain in other income.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None found attributing an IBKR reaction to other income. Adjusted EPS excludes currency-diversification and investment mark-to-market effects, so a GAAP other-income beat partly falls outside the bar the stock trades on.
findings.why_not_priced: Zacks' published line item ($30M) is well below both the stated Q2 underlying figure and the year-ago figure. If the market expected about $60M, that line would be published near it. Because the adjusted EPS bar strips part of this line, any beat transmits weakly.
findings.independence: GLOBAL -0.08% for the quarter, and a $307K mark-to-market loss on US government securities, from the September metrics release: https://finviz.com/news/397937/interactive-brokers-group-reports-brokerage-metrics-and-other-financial-information-for-september-2026-includes-reg-nms-execution-statistics. Consensus: https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/gear-interactive-brokers-ibkr-q3-121504839.html

findings.finding: The Fed hiked 25bp to 3.75-4.00% on 2026-09-16, and IBKR's own Q2 sensitivity is +$81M of annual NII per 25bp in Fed funds (plus $38M per 25bp across non-USD benchmarks). Q3 caught about two weeks of it. Q4 carries about +$20M a quarter, roughly 1% of revenue, which management will restate on the call. The prediction-market probability of a further hike at the Oct 27-28 meeting fell from 66% (Sept 28) to about 16% (Oct 7), which caps the forward story.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: IBKR gives no formal guidance; the rate-sensitivity statement on each call stands in for one. In 2025, cut-driven NII sensitivity was a recurring overhang. No reaction attributable to this line alone was found.
findings.why_not_priced: The hike is public, and Zacks' $1.12B NII consensus would include it for Q3. The unpriced part is only how management frames Q4 NII after the hike, given credit balances of $186.2B (+20% y/y). If the market had fully priced a rate tailwind, a rate-sensitive broker would not have fallen 5.9% on a rising-yield day (Sept 1) and another 4.8% on Oct 7.
findings.independence: Sensitivity of $81M per 25bp from the Q2 call: https://www.mitrade.com/insights/news/live-news/article-8-1923089-20260722. Hike confirmed by an economic calendar showing an actual of 4% against 3.75% previously: https://forexfundamentals.com/economic-calendar/fomc/2026-09-16. Odds of an October hike: https://defirate.com/odds/fed-decision/snapshot/2026-10-07T0500/. This is macro-to-company transmission using the company's own stated sensitivity.

findings.finding: Trading activity is decelerating into the call. DARTs growth fell from +27% y/y (July) and +23% (August) to +6% (September); September was -4% m/m, and the Q3 average (~4.27M) was about 11% below Q2's 4.82M. The VIX was 14.84 at the Oct 9 close (a low-vol, bullish regime), which points to subdued October activity if management gives October-to-date color on the call.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: This line moved the stock on monthly prints: -5.9% on 2026-09-01 (August DARTs -3% m/m plus yields) and -4.78% on 2026-10-07 (September DARTs, BMO trim). Q3 2025's -3.34% post-print move was attributed to growth concerns.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: the stock has already fallen on both monthly releases and sits 14% off its high. The residual is the October-to-date number given on the call, which nobody has yet. If it were priced, the put/call open-interest ratio would not be needed to express it and the stock would have stabilized. The low-VIX read is a proxy, not a company figure.
findings.independence: Market reaction to September's metrics: https://www.tradingkey.com/news/market-movers/262204268-market-movers-ibkr-20261007 (2026-10-07). VIX level: https://www.home.saxo/content/articles/options/the-middle-got-cheaper-the-edge-did-not---options-brief---12-october-2026-12102026. Robinhood's September 1-24 equity notional of ~$267B (about $15.7B a day against August's $16.0B ADV) shows flat retail activity: https://investors.robinhood.com/news-releases/news-release-details/robinhood-markets-inc-reports-august-2026-operating-data (peer, partly a proxy).

findings.finding: Margin loans ended Q3 at $105.2B, below Q2's quarter-end $108.5B (-3%), and fell to about 10.9% of client equity from the 11.7% high in Q2. Q3's average balance (~$103B) is still above Q2's average of $96.6B, so Q3 NII is supported, but Q4 starts from a lower exit run-rate than Q2 implied.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Margin-loan growth (+67% y/y in Q2) was a headline bull point last quarter, and the stock still fell 0.97%. No isolated reaction was found.
findings.why_not_priced: The monthly metrics show it, but headlines lead with '+36% y/y' (Sept) rather than the sequential decline from June's quarter-end. If it were priced, previews would flag a sequential margin-balance decline. None found do; Zacks called margin loans the fastest-growing metric.
findings.independence: September margin loans $105.2B: https://finviz.com/news/397937/interactive-brokers-group-reports-brokerage-metrics-and-other-financial-information-for-september-2026-includes-reg-nms-execution-statistics. Q2's 11.7% ratio: https://datalab.financemagnates.com/market-insights/interactive-brokers-margin-loans-up-67-interest-margin-down-to-1-93. The rate hike finding offsets this on forward NII; they are different drivers (balance against rate) and are kept apart.

findings.finding: Account growth held at +35% y/y through Q3. Accounts reached 5.576M in September, against about 5.2M at Q2's end, so roughly 370K net new accounts in the quarter, in line with or above Q2's pace. This answers the 'growth concerns' that drove the -3.34% post-print move in Q3 2025.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 2025 fell 3.34% after a beat, on growth-moderation worries; account growth is the line the bull case rests on.
findings.why_not_priced: It is pre-released monthly, so it is largely priced. It is filed because previews focus on the DARTs slowdown rather than the account line.

findings.finding: Positioning is washed-out going in: -14.2% from the $98.75 52-week high, -4.69% over 20 days (a 30-day decline of 8.6% per Zacks/Nasdaq), and put/call open interest of 1.69. The average analyst target is $105.84 even after BMO's trim. Short interest is low (2.3%), so the asymmetry comes from sentiment, not a squeeze.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The two beats that were sold (Jul 2026 -0.97%, Oct 2025 -3.34%) came after strong run-ups. The +6.0% in January 2026 followed a period of softer sentiment. That is weak evidence.
findings.why_not_priced: Positioning is the price itself. This is filed for the panel because it changes how the beat-selling history should be read. If the market were complacent, the stock would sit near its highs with call open interest dominant; it is the opposite.
findings.independence: The baseline's run-up and open-interest figures (sealed file). The Zacks note of a -3.8% month against a +2.4% S&P is in the Yahoo/Zacks article: https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/gear-interactive-brokers-ibkr-q3-121504839.html

baseline_tension: The findings net to roughly zero and fit the 'balanced' priced lean and the mild +1.6 skew. The 20-day decline and put-heavy open interest argue weakly against selling the beat this time, and nothing cuts strongly against the option market.
lessons_applied: Rule 1 (a verified fact is not a predicted reaction; this name sold its last two beats): the commission-upside finding was cut from +0.4 to +0.2.
Rule 2 (one-offs): other income is partly stripped from the adjusted EPS bar, so it was filed as one_off and cut from +0.3 to +0.15.
Rule 5 (macro transmission is a proxy): the rate-hike finding was cut from +0.4 to +0.3, since the falling odds of an October hike were already public.

Rule 5: the DARTs deceleration rests on company data, but the October part is a VIX proxy and partly priced after the Oct 7 fall; it moved from -0.6 to -0.5. Rule 7: short interest was checked (2.3%, not crowded), so there was no squeeze haircut.
Positioning was cut from +0.3 to +0.2 because it argues against the beat-selling history rather than with a document.
Account growth is pre-released and inside what the market saw monthly, so it went toward zero, from +0.2 to +0.1.
Margin-loan finding left standing at -0.3. p_up moved from 52 to 51; abs_move_pct is unchanged at 5.0.
